title: How would you evolve an API without breaking old clients?
description: Learn API versioning strategies, backward-compatible design rules, and a safe deprecation process that keeps old clients working while you ship new features.

data.text: APIs are contracts. Once a client depends on a response shape or behavior, changing it without coordination causes outages. The goal is to evolve the system without forcing every consumer to update at the same time.

cards.title: URL versioning
cards.description: Prefix the path with a version, such as /v1/users and /v2/users.
cons: Every new version is a breaking change by definition

cards.title: Header versioning
cards.description: Send the version in a custom header or Accept header.
cons: Harder to test in a browser
Caching proxies must be configured carefully

cards.title: No explicit versioning
cards.description: Add fields and deprecate old ones without versioned paths.
pros: Easiest for mobile apps that auto-update
cons: Harder to remove old fields safely

data.title: Safe change checklist
items: Add new fields without removing old ones
Make previously required fields optional only after a deprecation period
Never change the type of an existing field
Keep error codes stable so clients can branch on them
Document every change and the minimum client version required

data.title: Deprecation is a process, not an event
data.text: Announce deprecations early, provide migration guides, and give clients a realistic timeline. Removing a field without warning is a breaking change, even if your tests pass.

data.title: Adding a field safely
data.content: You need to add a phone number to the user profile response. Add the new field as optional. Old clients ignore it. New clients read it if present. After one release cycle, make it required and remove the old fallback path.

data.title: Key takeaway
points: Additive changes are safe; removals and renames are breaking
Version explicitly when you cannot keep old fields forever
Document deprecation timelines and communicate them to consumers
